title: The Mask in the Mirror
subtitle: Between two mirrors hangs a single object. One face, two faces ... cascading into the infinite.

trails.title: A Tattered Invitation
trails.description: A serpent brings an apple—but I already possess the wisdom.

content.text:
Dear Mr. Aleph,

The National Foucault Studies Association extends a formal invitation for you to join our organization. Our mission is to guide society and the world toward a more structured and enlightened future. We believe your exceptional abilities will be instrumental in achieving this vision. We eagerly await your response.

Sincerely,
José Tartuffe
Comala Prison, Ushuaia

trails.title: Draft of a Strange Incantation
trails.description: The greatest arcane skills demand thorough preparation. Every list is the crystallization of countless insights.

content.text:
Regarding the ... (blurred by water stains) ritual:

1. A large number of Arcanists—this should be an easily achievable goal for Manus Vindictae. Young people capable of lifting bricks and setting sail are plentiful. Devotion remains the best catalyst.

2. Roar Lion's Tail, Sacred Scarab Wings, Nukutaeao Shell—when combined with the Fountain of Immortality, it seems likely that Manus Vindictae aims to achieve something extraordinary. Given the shell's properties, it can withstand an immense amount of energy, ensuring the ritual's success. This is indeed an incantation requiring considerable meticulous preparation.

3. The location ... (blurred by water stains)—remains an excellent choice, but for the ritual itself, timing is of paramount importance. The "time" referred to here is not our traditional understanding, but time "itself."

items.text: The Mask in the Mirror

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where did the Physician go? Wait.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sir, are you ...?
No one notices when the unfamiliar prisoner appears.
He seems calm and almost ordinary, like an unchanging mirror that has stood here all along—in this room, in this labyrinth, passed unseen by everyone.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: *pant*
The answer she now sees plainly makes her step back in a panic.
But in the end, she says the name out loud. Its sound is heavy, cold, and leaves her at a loss.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Aleph.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's you, my pen pal.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You are in fact in Comala.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: All those letters, all the ideas we shared—they weren't just my imagination or some prank. Vertin, Sonetto, it's all just as I told you!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: They weren't meaningless. *pant* They're all real.
Yet, why does she feel no joy?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So, sir, are you Aleph, the ruler of this prison?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you the one controlling the Panopticon with a die? The one hiding Ms. Dores's whereabouts?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: What curious inquiries, quite different from the last 2666 questions I've received.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: My guests, you may call me Aleph, or by any other name, be it a symbol of god's oneness or a farcical epithet.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I am merely one of the many prisoners who voluntarily reside here—a single letter in the alphabet of the Panopticon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A letter ... The way you speak is quite different from Dr. Merlin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Still, I wonder what your relationship is with him.
Under the dim lighting, the man looks drained of all energy.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But allow me to make a guess: You're Dr. Merlin, aren't you?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I'm afraid that's not entirely accurate, but you may think of it that way.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Merlin is a figment born of my mind, an incomplete reenactment. He is me, yes, but not entirely.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: He—or rather, they—failed to find their answers.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: They fought against their predestined fates, only to be inevitably crushed under their weight. I simply stood by and watched it all unfold. That was the extent of our relationship.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "They"?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: You've already met Merlin and the Idealist—even witnessed their demise.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Shackled by the delusions of verses, the Idealist lost his own name. Merlin, too, imprisoned himself within the system of the Panopticon.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I'm sure their desperate pursuits caused you some trouble.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Please forgive them. After all, your fleeting encounters led to the demise of them both.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think I understand now. The Idealist and the Physician are both parts of you, or, to put it another way, they're your alter egos.
It seems the jailer's diagnosis, that the whole prison is mad, has been shown to be more accurate than anyone could have imagined.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The Physician mentioned Manus Vindictae. What's the relationship between this prison and the Manus?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Visitors from the Foundation, we all witnessed those eras perish.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: In 1977, not long before the fourth "Storm," I arrived in Ushuaia. Shortly after, some members of the National Foucault Studies Association reached out to me.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: But it wasn't just them. An arcanist organization called Manus Vindictae also approached me. Each of them wanted answers. They named me their "advisor."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You acted as an "advisor" to the Manus?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: The two parties presented me with a concept and a parable, respectively.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: A concept and a parable?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: The Foucault Association sought to explore the feasibility of the Panopticon concept here.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: While Manus Vindictae showed me a parable of the past and future.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Day and night, I wandered through endless texts, endless realities, as I searched for answers. And thus, Merlin was born. He was both an experiment and a price I paid.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: A new concept, a new direction ... Pursuing such things always leaves me confined by the limitations of human knowledge.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Merlin spent his entire life exploring Foucault's theories in pursuit of that singular yet infinite answer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What about the Manus, Mr. Aleph? You didn't explain why you helped them.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Explain why?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Because they asked me to, just as you have.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I simply worked to answer their questions.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So you're saying that, to you, we're no different from Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And if we ask, you'll answer us, without holding anything back?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Is that not precisely what is happening this very moment?
Aleph picks up the fallen die. It flickers with a familiar, comforting glow.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text:
This is what the Manus gave Merlin, a magical die named the 
Tear of Comala.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: It was once a gemstone that belonged to a god. At the beginning of the century, explorers plucked it from an ancient gate they discovered in Antarctica.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: To the explorers' amazement, the gemstone could turn human desires into reality.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: So, they cut it into a die, a symbol of fate, and used it to build a sanatorium, which was later transformed into the Panopticon you are standing in right now.
His words are direct, yet they still leave the outsiders perplexed.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Then, Aleph, you really are the mastermind behind the Panopticon?
The silent girl grips her notebook. Her knuckles turn white from the pressure.
The draft of an unpublished novel, with words that only she knows—the countless hours spent at her desk, the self-reflections, the meticulous questioning, revisions, and scrutiny of every word.
That book holds the life of its writer.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You said Merlin used the Panopticon to seek his answer. W-What does that have to do with my novel?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I don't get it, Aleph. Why would you use my novel to manipulate this place?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Roberta, García, Octavia, Pablo, the jailer, everyone ... Not one of them deserved to be trapped in a deadly loop in which everyone's fate is already predestined.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: They're just like the ghosts in Amalfitano, inescapably trapped within the ruins.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Tell me, what is it you really want?
Hearing this, the lonely prisoner fidgets with the die, looking puzzled.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: It's not about what I want. It's about what you want.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: The third line of your first letter.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: You said you wanted to give The Rise and Fall of Sanity an ending.
